parsed.explanation: Nepal is comparatively progressive in South Asia. The 2007 Supreme Court Sunil Babu Pant ruling recognized a third gender, the 2015 constitution explicitly references gender and sexual minorities, and citizenship documents with an 'O' marker have been issued. Pant was an elected parliamentarian, and major parties have generally not run anti-trans platforms. Mainstream politicians rarely use overt anti-trans rhetoric. However, uncertainty remains. Implementation is patchy, the state has been slow to legislate same-sex marriage and full legal gender recognition, and conservative and religious-nationalist factions (including Hindu-state advocates) can be unsympathetic. Some local officials and police harass trans people. Politicians are mostly indifferent or neglectful rather than actively hostile, but that indifference is not the same as support. Trans people who do not fit the third-gender category, such as trans men and those wanting a binary marker, are less well served.
